newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen down sharply due to BOJ comments.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen down sharply due to BOJ comments.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen futures fell sharply in mid-morning trade on Wednesday due to comments by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita that a prolonged easy monetary policy was responsible for Japan's "bubble" economy of the 1980s.
"The market seemed to pay some respect to the governor's comments, and euroyen futures were sold," said a trader for a major brokerage house.
The December stood at 98.88 as of 0117 GMT, down sharply from the previous day's settlement of 98.94.

Speaking at a parliamentary committee meeting, BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday the BOJ should carry out monetary policy with the aim of achieving sustainable economic growth without inflation.
He said the BOJ would take steps pre-emptively to achieve this goal.

Matsushita also said the central bank's policy in the late 1980s, when it took an easy monetary stance for a prolonged period, was one factor which brought about the so-called "bubble" economy of inflated asset prices.

Recent rises in Tokyo share prices have led to concerns that the BOJ may raise interest rates earlier than previously expected, but there is still scepticism about the feasibility of possible credit-tightening, the brokerage house trader said.
"The market is still not sure whether the economy's recovery is full-blown... The market has not yet gone so far as to factor in a possible rise in the official discount rate," the trader said.
If share prices continue to be firm, the BOJ may decide to raise short-term interest rates, but the central bank is unlikely to raise the official discount rate anytime soon, the trader added.
The BOJ is unlikely to consider a change in monetary policy until it views forthcoming economic data for the April-June period, the city bank trader said.
The BOJ refrained from its regular 0020 GMT operation this morning.
The money market had a fund surplus of 280 billion yen going into the day.

The key unsecured overnight call rate was mostly traded at 0.50 percent on Wednesday morning, up from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.49 percent, as demand for short-term funds remained strong, traders said.
No new certificates of deposit (CDs) had been issued as of 0313 GMT. The key three-month CDs were offered at 0.57 percent.
In the interest rate swap market, there was talk during the morning that an investment bank was receiving long-term fixed interest rates, a trust bank trader said.
The 10-year interest rate swap rate was quoted at 2.91/95 percent as of 0315 GMT, up from 2.88/92 percent on Tuesday.
